subject.title: fix(ui): preserve login across same-origin gateways

question: Should the endpoint-scoped browser device-credential migration be accepted as the upgrade behavior for existing unscoped `openclaw.device.auth.v1` records?
rationale: The code and tests support the fix, but the PR intentionally changes credential persistence and legacy cleanup semantics, which is a maintainer-owned compatibility/security tradeoff.

options.title: Accept scoped migration
options.body: Merge after exact-head gates pass, treating first-gateway legacy claim and deletion as the intended upgrade behavior.

options.title: Require live upgrade proof
options.body: Ask for a browser-profile upgrade transcript showing the legacy key migrating to one scoped key before merge.

options.title: Pause for another policy
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want a different legacy credential retention or recovery policy.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped migration
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head gates pass, treating first-gateway legacy claim and deletion as the intended upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest prior maintainer-visible auth-storage policy decision is the merged refresh-auth work and no-cross-tab-token follow-up discussion.
